result:
I've written the recommendation below. I didn't fit or inspect anything, and the repo holds no data, so every fact comes from your description. My one assumption about the analysis folder name is `water-reports-trial/`.

**Main points**

- **Use the randomization.** The random draw of 12 of the 24 towns makes this a cluster-randomized trial. The primary design is a comparison of the 12 report towns with the 12 control towns over March 2025 to February 2026, adjusted for each town's own baseline use. For the board's question, this is plausibly identified.
- **Don't use the analyst's before/after comparison as the main analysis.** The July 2025 drought order, seasonal patterns and long-run trends all change at about the same time as the reports. A before/after comparison in the report towns cannot separate the reports from those changes. The control towns, which faced the same drought, are what make the comparison work.
- **Don't control for rebate sign-up.** Sign-up happened after the reports started and was higher in report towns, so it is probably one way the reports reduced use. Controlling for it would remove part of the effect the board asked about.
- **The standard errors won't be tiny.** Treatment was assigned to 24 towns, not to 2.1 million meter reads. The effective sample is 12 towns against 12. Inference must work at the town level. I recommend exact randomization inference over all 2,704,156 possible draws of 12 towns from 24.

**File: `water-reports-trial/causal-design.md`**

```markdown
# Causal design: monthly home water-use reports, 24-town trial

Status: pre-estimation recommendation. No data inspected, no models fitted, no
diagnostics run. All facts below come from the project description given on
2026-11-12 unless labeled "assumed".

## 1. Decision and requested estimand

**Recommendation:** analyze the trial as a **cluster-randomized experiment**.
Compare the 12 randomly assigned report towns with the 12 control towns over
March 2025–February 2026, adjusting for pre-period (March 2023–February 2025)
use. Run inference at the town level by randomization inference. Do **not** use
a before/after comparison within report towns as the primary design. Do **not**
adjust for rebate sign-up.

- **Requested causal question:**
  - *Intervention:* mailing a monthly neighbor-comparison report to every
    household in a town, from March 2025.
  - *Comparator:* no new communication.
  - *Outcome:* household metered water use.
  - *Population:* households in the trial towns.
  - *Time zero:* March 2025, the first mailing.
  - *Horizon:* 12 months (March 2025–February 2026).
  - *Contrast:* mean difference in household use. A relative (%) difference is
    secondary.
  - *Decision:* whether reports reduce use. Whether this informs a rollout to
    the other 34 towns is assumed, not stated (§9).
- **Requested estimand:** the intention-to-treat (ITT) effect of *mailing* the
  reports.
  - *Plain language:* the difference between (a) average monthly household use
    over March 2025–February 2026 had the trial towns' households been mailed
    reports and (b) the same average had they not been.
  - *Primary version:* averaged over households in the 24 randomized towns
    (household-weighted).
  - *Board wording:* "in the trial towns" may mean only the 12 report towns
    (an ATT). Because those 12 were a random draw from the 24, the same design
    targets it under the same assumptions. Confirm which wording the board
    means (§9).
  - *Reading vs mailing:* this is the effect of being mailed reports, not of
    reading them.
- **Design status:** `plausibly identified`.
  - *Why:* town-level random assignment by draw; a no-opt-out offer; outcomes
    metered for all households in both arms; an untreated randomized
    comparison exposed to the same drought order.
  - *Remaining gates (routine, §4/§6):* confirm the randomization record; rule
    out co-interventions that differed by arm; confirm outcome completeness
    and household composition.
- **Estimands that are not identified, or not requested:**
  - *Effect of reading the reports:* `not identified`. Reading is not recorded.
    There is no instrument-based receipt analysis without a receipt measure.
  - *Effect in all 58 towns, or in the 34 non-trial towns:* not identified by
    this trial alone. The trial towns were selected for having smart meters.
    Transport needs evidence on effect modifiers and support (§5).
  - *Effect of reports in a non-drought year:* this trial ran with a drought
    order in place from July 2025. The estimated effect is conditional on that
    context.
- **Recommendation-changing conditions:**
  - Assignment was not a single clean draw (for example a re-draw, or towns
    swapped after the draw): status becomes `conditional` pending a review of
    the assignment record.
  - The utility enforced the drought order or marketed rebates differently in
    report towns, or the reports themselves carried drought or rebate content:
    the estimand becomes a bundled-intervention effect, which must be agreed
    with the board.
  - Material missing reads or household turnover that differs by arm: add an
    outcome-observation analysis before estimation.

Sources: Hernán and Robins (2020), on randomized experiments, ITT and
consistency (https://miguelhernan.org/whatifbook).

## 2. Design and data inventory

| Fact | Known/assumed/unknown | Evidence/source | Implication/action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 24 of 58 towns eligible because they have smart meters | Known | Description | Trial population = smart-meter towns. Not a sample of all 58 |
| 12 of 24 assigned to reports by a random draw | Known | Description | Primary identifying variation. Obtain the draw record (method, seed/witness, date) |
| Draw was unstratified simple random selection of 12 of 24 | Assumed | None | If stratified/paired, randomization inference must permute within strata |
| Unit of assignment = town; towns ≥10 miles apart, separate communities | Known | Description | 24 independent assignments. Household reads are not independent assignments |
| Every household in report towns mailed monthly from March 2025; no opt-out | Known | Description | ITT of mailing is well defined. Check mailing logs, returned mail, new accounts added to the mailing list |
| Whether reports were read | Unknown (not recorded) | Description | Receipt effect not identified |
| Control towns got nothing new from the trial | Known | Description | Confirm no other utility communication differed by arm |
| Monthly meter reads, all households in 24 towns, Mar 2023–Feb 2026 (~2.1M reads) | Known | Description | 24 pre-months support baseline adjustment and placebo periods. Confirm read dates vs consumption periods, estimated reads, meter replacements |
| Read "March 2025" measures consumption after first mailing | Unknown | None | Define time zero by mailing date and read consumption window. The first post read may be partly pre-treatment |
| Household size and lot size from billing | Known; measurement date unknown | Description | Use only values recorded before March 2025 as baseline covariates |
| Drought order limiting lawn watering, July 2025, all 58 towns | Known | Description | Common shock to both arms. Not a confounder of the randomized comparison, but it fatally confounds a pre/post design. Effect is drought-context-specific |
| Enforcement/communication of drought order uniform across towns | Assumed | None | If enforcement differed by arm → co-intervention (§4) |
| Low-flow fixture rebate sign-ups higher in report towns | Known (direction); sign-up dates unknown | Description | Post-treatment, likely mediator. Exclude from adjustment; analyze as secondary outcome |
| Rebate offered equally in all 24 towns, not promoted in reports | Assumed | None | If promoted in reports, rebate is part of the intervention bundle |
| Missing reads, account openings/closures, move-ins/outs by arm | Unknown | None | Define cohort and check composition/missingness by arm (§4, §6) |
| Households per town | Unknown | None | Unequal town sizes affect household- vs town-weighting and precision |
| Spillover between towns (media, shared employers, word of mouth) | Assumed small | Distance/separate communities | Would bias the ITT toward zero. Ask about press coverage |

No data were inspected. Required data: household-month reads with read dates
and consumption periods, read type (actual/estimated), account open/close
dates, town ID, arm, baseline household size and lot size with record dates,
mailing logs, rebate sign-up dates, and the randomization record.

## 3. Causal structure and adjustment

Nodes (t = month; pre = Mar 2023–Feb 2025, post = Mar 2025–Feb 2026):

- R: town assignment by random draw (Feb/Mar 2025)
- M: reports mailed (post). M = R by design, with no opt-out
- Read: household reads report (post, unobserved)
- Rb: rebate sign-up (post)
- D: drought order (Jul 2025, all towns)
- W: weather/season (all months)
- X: baseline household size, lot size, pre-period use Y_pre
- U: unobserved town and household factors (income, garden type, local norms)
- Y: post-period household monthly use
- S: household observed in post period (account active, read recorded)

Edge list:

- R → M → Read → Y. Read → Rb → Y. M → Rb (via reports, if rebate mentioned).
- U → X, U → Y_pre, U → Y, U → Rb.
- X → Y.
- D → Y, W → Y (common to both arms). No edge R → D or D → R (absent-edge
  assumption: drought order was not caused by or targeted using assignment).
- U → R: **absent by randomization**. This is the key defended absent edge.
- M → S? and Y → S? (disputed: reports could affect moving/closure or
  estimated reads. Plausibly negligible but must be checked).
- Utility enforcement E → Y with R → E: **assumed absent** (no differential
  co-intervention). Must be audited.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R[Random town assignment] --> M[Reports mailed]
    M --> Rd[Read report - unobserved]
    Rd --> Y[Post-period use]
    Rd --> Rb[Rebate sign-up - post]
    M -.-> Rb
    Rb --> Y
    U[Unobserved town/household factors] --> X[Baseline size, lot, Y_pre]
    U --> Y
    U --> Rb
    X --> Y
    D[Drought order Jul 2025] --> Y
    W[Weather/season] --> Y
    M -.disputed.-> S[Observed in post?]
    Y -.disputed.-> S
```

**Proposed adjustment set:** none required for identification; randomization
blocks U → R. For precision, adjust only for pre-treatment variables: town or
household pre-period use (Y_pre) and baseline household size and lot size.

**Excluded:**
- Rebate sign-up (Rb): a post-treatment mediator. Conditioning on it removes
  the part of the report effect that works through fixture upgrades, and may
  open U → Rb ← M (collider bias).
- Any post-March-2025 covariates.
- Drought indicators: common to both arms. They add no identification, and
  calendar effects are absorbed by comparing arms within the same months.

**Mediators/colliders:** Read and Rb are mediators. S is a potential selection
node; complete-case analysis conditions on S.

**Design restrictions not encoded in the graph:** no differential
co-interventions by arm (enforcement, rebate marketing, other utility
messaging); no interference across towns; a single defined version of the
report.

**Why the analyst's pre/post design fails:** in a within-report-town
before/after comparison, D, W and secular trends all change between pre and
post. Every one is a backdoor-free but non-separable cause of the change in Y,
and the design has no untreated comparison to remove them. The drought order
(July 2025) falls inside the post window. That is exactly the coinciding-shock
case in which interrupted-time-series designs are not identified without a
control series (Lopez Bernal et al. 2017,
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5407170/).

## 4. Identification assumptions and evidence

| Assumption | Why needed | Supporting evidence | Planned challenge/sensitivity | Untestable remainder / gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Randomization: assignment independent of potential outcomes | Identifies ITT without confounding adjustment | Random draw of 12/24 (described) | Obtain draw record; check no re-draws/swaps; baseline balance on 24 months of pre-use (§6) | Balance is supporting only. Gate: draw record must exist and match arm list |
| Consistency: one "mailing" intervention | Defines the estimand | Uniform monthly mailing, no opt-out | Mailing logs: coverage, returned mail, months missed, content changes | Changes in report design mid-trial are part of the intervention as delivered |
| No differential co-intervention | Otherwise the effect is a bundle | None yet | Audit drought enforcement, rebate marketing, other utility messages by arm | Gate: if present, redefine as bundled estimand or stop |
| No interference between towns | Control towns represent "no reports" | ≥10 miles, separate communities | Ask about press/social-media coverage; optional distance check | Untestable in full; bias would be toward zero |
| Outcome observation/composition | Compare the same population | Smart meters on all households | Missing/estimated reads, account turnover by arm and month | If differential: cohort definition, sensitivity, bounds |
| Positivity | Both arms observed | 12 vs 12 by design | — | Satisfied by design at town level |

**Identified target under these assumptions:** the household-averaged ITT of
mailing in the 24 trial towns over March 2025–February 2026, under the
drought-year conditions that applied.

**Identification ≠ precision.** With 12 towns per arm, precision is limited by
between-town variation. The 2.1 million reads improve within-town measurement,
not the number of independent assignments. Standard errors from household-level
models that treat reads as independent will be far too small.

## 5. Candidate comparison and primary choice

| Candidate | Identified estimand | Match to requested target | Critical assumptions | Required data | Main threat | Feasibility / failure action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Cluster-randomized ITT with baseline adjustment (primary)** | ITT of mailing, 24 towns, 12-month horizon | Direct | Randomization, no differential co-intervention, outcome observation, no cross-town interference | Reads Mar 2023–Feb 2026, arm, town, baseline covariates | Few clusters → wide intervals; co-intervention | Feasible now. If co-intervention found, redefine bundle or stop |
| B. Randomized difference-in-differences / event study (24 towns) | Same ITT, plus month-by-month path | Direct; robustness and dynamics | As A; pre-period trends supported by randomization rather than assumed | Same | Less efficient than baseline adjustment if pre/post correlation is not high; same few-cluster issue | Secondary analysis; report dynamic path (pre-July vs post-July drought) as prespecified exploration |
| C. Analyst's within-report-town before/after with household size, lot size, rebate controls | Pre/post change in report towns | **Not identified** for the requested effect | Requires no drought, season, trend or other change — contradicted by the July 2025 order | Report-town reads only | Drought/season/trend confounding; rebate adjustment blocks part of the effect; spurious precision | Do not use. Retain only as descriptive context, clearly labeled |

**Primary:** A.

**Weakest assumption:** no differential co-intervention by arm. The higher
rebate sign-up in report towns is consistent with a mediated report effect, but
also with differential rebate promotion.

**Fallback:** B, which identifies the same ITT under randomization. If
differential composition or missingness appears, use a fixed baseline cohort
with sensitivity bounds.

**Separate, not requested:** a 58-town or 34-town rollout effect. This needs a
transport analysis (comparison of smart-meter versus non-smart-meter towns on
effect modifiers) or a new randomized rollout. It is not part of this
recommendation.

## 6. Diagnostic, falsification and sensitivity plan

All items are **planned**; none performed.

| Check | Data needed | Assumption challenged | Limitation | Action if it fails |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Randomization record audit | Draw method, date, witness/seed, arm list | Randomization | Cannot detect an undocumented manipulation | No record or swaps → status `conditional`; review with the person who drew |
| Baseline balance: town mean use Mar 2023–Feb 2025, household size, lot size | Pre-period reads, billing | Randomization (chance imbalance) | Balance does not prove exchangeability on unobservables; with 12 vs 12, chance imbalance is expected | Baseline adjustment already planned; report imbalance |
| Placebo period: apply the primary estimator to Mar 2024–Feb 2025 as if treated | Pre-period reads | Estimator/specification; pre-existing arm differences | A null placebo is not proof | Investigate specification; report |
| Co-intervention audit: drought enforcement actions, rebate marketing, other mailings by town | Utility operations records | No differential co-intervention | Missing records ≠ none | Redefine estimand as bundle or stop |
| Mailing delivery audit | Mailing logs, returned mail | Consistency | Delivery ≠ reading | Report delivered share; ITT stands |
| Outcome completeness and composition by arm and month (missing reads, estimated reads, account opens/closes) | Read flags, account dates | Outcome observation | Equal rates ≠ ignorable missingness | Fixed March-2025 cohort analysis; sensitivity/bounds |
| Rebate sign-up as secondary outcome (ITT on sign-up) | Sign-up dates | Mechanism description | Not a mediation analysis | Report descriptively; formal mediation needs a separate design |
| Drought-period split (Mar–Jun vs Jul 2025–Feb 2026), prespecified | Reads | Effect heterogeneity with drought | 12 vs 12 → low power; exploratory | Report as exploratory only |
| Specification sensitivity: town-weighted vs household-weighted; absolute vs log/ratio scale; winsorized extreme users | Reads | Robustness of the summary | Agreement does not validate identification | Report range; keep prespecified primary |
| Inference sensitivity: randomization inference vs small-cluster-corrected town-clustered SEs / wild cluster bootstrap | Town-level data | Inference validity with 24 clusters | Different procedures make different assumptions | Report the randomization-inference result as primary |

Passing balance and placebo checks supports, but cannot prove, the absence of
co-interventions or interference.

## 7. Implementation handoff

- **Estimand:** household-weighted ITT of mailing reports on mean monthly
  household water use, March 2025–February 2026, in the 24 randomized towns.
  - Primary scale: mean difference (gallons per household per day or per
    month; confirm unit).
  - Secondary: percent difference relative to the control-arm mean.
  - Report-town ATT: same estimator, labeled.
- **Sample:**
  - Primary cohort: households with an active account on the first mailing
    date (March 2025).
  - Secondary: all households active in each month.
  - Exclude non-residential accounts (assumed out of scope; confirm).
- **Keys and roles:**
  - Keys: town_id (cluster, assignment unit), household/account_id,
    read_period (consumption window start/end).
  - Assignment: arm (report/control).
  - Outcome: metered use per period, with an estimated-read flag.
  - Baseline covariates (pre-March 2025 values only): Y_pre, household_size,
    lot_size.
  - Post-treatment, not adjusted: rebate_signup and its date.
- **Time zero:** first mailing date. Assign read periods to post only when the
  consumption window begins on or after it. Handle straddling periods by
  exclusion or proration (prespecify).
- **Primary estimator:**
  - Difference in household-weighted post-period mean use between arms,
    adjusted for baseline use.
  - Option 1: town-level ANCOVA of post-period mean on pre-period mean.
  - Option 2: household-level regression with Y_pre, household_size and
    lot_size, aggregated to a town-level estimate.
  - Prespecify one before seeing outcomes.
- **Inference:**
  - Exact randomization inference over all C(24,12) = 2,704,156 assignments
    (permute within strata if the draw was stratified).
  - Confidence interval by test inversion under a stated constant-additive-
    effect assumption.
  - Sensitivity: small-cluster-corrected town-clustered errors (≈22 degrees
    of freedom).
  - No household- or read-level iid standard errors.
- **Secondary:**
  - Randomized event study by month (candidate B).
  - ITT on rebate sign-up.
  - Prespecified drought-period split.
  - Multiplicity: label all secondary analyses exploratory.
- **Gates (stop or revise before estimating):**
  - Randomization record missing or inconsistent.
  - Differential co-intervention found.
  - Differential outcome missingness or composition beyond the planned
    sensitivity analyses.
- **Tools:** Polars for profiling. A design-based frequentist analysis is
  sufficient. Bayesian execution is not required. An optional hierarchical
  town model would go through `recommend-probabilistic-model`, with this memo
  as its identification input.
- **Output:**
  - ITT with randomization p-value and CI.
  - Balance table and placebo-period result.
  - Co-intervention, mailing and composition audits.
  - Claim limits: 24 smart-meter towns, a drought year, the effect of mailing
    not reading, not a 58-town effect.

## 8. Sources

- Hernán, M. A., and J. M. Robins (2020). *Causal Inference: What If* —
  randomized experiments, ITT, consistency, exchangeability, selection.
  https://miguelhernan.org/whatifbook
- Lopez Bernal, J., S. Cummins, A. Gasparrini (2017). Interrupted time series
  regression for the evaluation of public health interventions: a tutorial —
  concurrent shocks and the need for a control series (why candidate C fails).
  https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5407170/
- Callaway, B., and P. H. C. Sant'Anna (2021). Difference-in-Differences with
  Multiple Time Periods — group/time ATT framing for candidate B.
  https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.09015

Source gap: specific references for randomization inference and small-cluster
variance corrections in cluster-randomized trials have not been verified in
this session. Add verified primary sources before finalizing the analysis plan.

## 9. Open questions and next action

| Question | Who/what can answer | Effect on recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| Does "the trial towns" mean all 24 or the 12 report towns? Is the decision a rollout to the other 34? | Board | Changes the labeled estimand (ITT vs ATT). A rollout question needs transport evidence |
| How exactly was the draw done (simple vs stratified/paired, re-draws, record)? | Whoever ran the draw | Inference structure; status if no record |
| Did reports mention the drought order or the rebate? Was the rebate promoted differently by town? | Program staff | Bundle definition; co-intervention gate |
| Was drought enforcement uniform across the 24 towns? | Operations | Co-intervention gate |
| How do meter read dates map to consumption periods? Are estimated reads flagged? | Data owner | Time zero and outcome definition |
| Household counts per town; account turnover and missing reads by arm | Analyst (profiling) | Weighting, composition sensitivity |
| Any press/social-media coverage that reached control towns? | Communications | Interference (bias toward zero) |
| When were household size and lot size recorded? | Data owner | Whether they qualify as baseline covariates |

**Next action:** answer the questions above and pull the randomization record
and co-intervention records. Then start a fresh implementation session using
this memo as input: prespecify the primary estimator before looking at
post-period outcomes.
```

**Questions where I made assumptions** (also in §9 of the memo):

1. Does the board mean all 24 towns, or only the 12 report towns? Is the real decision whether to roll out to the other 34 towns?
2. Was the draw a simple pick of 12 from 24, or stratified or paired? Is there a written record of it?
3. Did the reports mention the drought or the rebate? Was the drought order enforced, or the rebate promoted, the same way in both arms?
4. How do meter read dates line up with consumption periods? When were household size and lot size recorded?

I suggest settling these, then starting a fresh session to implement the analysis from the memo.
